title: Cairn — Object Storage
description: Cairn single-node S3-compatible object storage: traffic, stored bytes and compression, the group-committing metadata writer, and asynchronous replication. Scraped from Cairn's Prometheus endpoint on :7373/metrics.

panels.title: Buckets
panels.description: Buckets on this node.

panels.title: Objects
panels.description: Current objects, excluding noncurrent versions.

panels.title: Stored on disk
panels.description: Physical bytes after compression — what actually occupies the filesystem.

panels.title: Compression saved
panels.description: Logical minus physical. Reads 0 for incompressible data, where the block container costs marginally more than it saves.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Requests/sec by surface: s3, api, web, share, and the health probes.

panels.title: Errors by status
panels.description: Only 4xx and 5xx. A rising 5xx line is the thing to alert on.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Object bytes leaving and entering the node.

panels.title: S3 latency
panels.description: Worst-case data-plane handling latency across methods, by quantile.

panels.title: Requests/sec
panels.description: All surfaces combined.

panels.title: Error ratio
panels.description: Share of requests that failed.

panels.title: 5xx/sec
panels.description: Server faults only — should sit at zero.

panels.title: Slowest route p99
panels.description: The worst p99 across every surface.

panels.title: By method
panels.description: The GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE/POST mix.

panels.title: All responses by status
panels.description: Every status, not just failures — the success baseline Overview omits.

panels.title: Mean latency by route
panels.description: Average handling time per surface (the quantiles live on Overview).

panels.title: Share-link responses
panels.description: Public /share/{token} traffic. 410 means expired or revoked, 404 an unknown token.

panels.title: Noncurrent versions
panels.description: Superseded versions still retained. Lifecycle rules expire these.

panels.title: Average object size
panels.description: Logical bytes per current object — small-object workloads stress metadata, not disk.

panels.title: Compression ratio
panels.description: Physical / logical. Below 1.0 means compression is winning.

panels.title: Logical bytes stored
panels.description: Bytes as clients see them, before compression. What this costs on disk is the 'Stored on disk' tile on Overview; the ratio between them is the tile to the left.

panels.title: Versions over time
panels.description: Total versions, current plus noncurrent. A rising line with a flat object count means superseded versions are accumulating — what lifecycle rules expire.

panels.title: Writer queue depth
panels.description: Mutations submitted but not yet committed. Sustained growth is write saturation.

panels.title: Commits/sec
panels.description: Group commits per second — each one is a durability barrier (fsync).

panels.title: WAL size
panels.description: Unbounded growth means a long-lived reader is starving the checkpointer.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Read-through config cache in front of SQLite.

panels.title: Group-commit duration
panels.description: Wall time of one metadata durability barrier.

panels.title: Group-commit batch size
panels.description: Mutations coalesced into each fsync — higher amortises the barrier better.

panels.title: Metadata cache traffic
panels.description: Raw hit and miss rates behind the ratio above.

panels.title: WAL checkpoints
panels.description: Truncating checkpoints are what keep the WAL bounded.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Terminally failed outbox entries, after the retry budget. Should be 0.

panels.title: Unreplicated
panels.description: Versions with no replica yet.

panels.title: Claimed
panels.description: Entries currently leased by a worker.

panels.title: Plaintext length mismatch
panels.description: Metadata-declared plaintext reads refused because file and logical lengths differ. Non-zero indicates missing/inconsistent metadata or truncated local storage.

panels.title: Replication lag
panels.description: Age of the oldest entry still owed. Cross-host redundancy is asynchronous, so this is the observable window of exposure.

panels.title: Outbox depth
panels.description: Entries due for shipping. Draining to zero is healthy; a rising floor is not.
